summary:
AstroBio Sentinel is an offline, human-governed health decision-support dashboard built for astronauts on deep-space missions, such as the Ares IV transit to Mars. Because signals between Earth and Mars face a one-way communication delay of 8 to 20 minutes, crews cannot rely on real-time ground doctors and opaque "black-box" AI systems pose serious automation risks. Our interface solves this by separating simulated crew telemetry, live NASA space-weather feeds, and peer-reviewed research in one calm view. Rather than diagnosing conditions or prescribing treatments autonomously, it pairs crew vitals and closed-loop microalgae life-support metrics with explicit scientific boundaries, keeping medical authority firmly in human hands.

In conclusion, AstroBio Sentinel directly fulfills the NASA Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge by transforming complex human spaceflight hazards into an intuitive, color-coded self-assessment workflow. Combining dynamic physiological trends, routine crew action prompts, gamified bio-dome stewardship, and transparent scientific boundaries, it empowers crews to evaluate and act on their health independently while offering sustainable dual-use benefits for rural clinics and microalgae biotechnology in Sarawak.
details:
Syfra Team's Project Solution

AstroBio Sentinel is an offline, interactive astronaut health decision support platform designed to help deep space crews monitor their physical and behavioral health while managing closed-loop microalgae life support. Turning real NASA Human Research Program (HRP) frameworks, Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) studies, and live DONKI space-weather feeds into a calm, traceable mission dashboard, the platform guides astronauts through daily self-assessments and emergency countermeasures across an 8 minute, 41 second (and up to 20-minute) Earth to Mars communication delay, keeping every medical decision firmly in human hands.

Companion Resources & Live Prototype

• Interactive Health Dashboard (Figma Prototype)

• Mission Overview & Audio Transmission Log (Framer)

How Does Our Solution Work

Inside the interface, the user steps into the role of Cmdr. Zahra Noor (Avatar), Flight Engineer aboard the Ares IV Mars Transit on Mission Day 184. Instead of overwhelming the crew with opaque "black-box" AI diagnoses, AstroBio Sentinel guides the user through a transparent, step-by-step operational workflow:

1. Daily Guided Self-Assessment & Crew Action Queue:

At the start of a mission cycle, the dashboard greets the commander with a single calm metric: 92% Symbiosis (combining 92% Human Readiness and 87% Algae Bioreactor Health).

Through the Crew Action Queue (Now / Next / Review / Support), the user is prompted to complete routine checks such as blood pressure, private mood check-ins, and scheduled hydration accompanied by a plain language visual crew guide so no astronaut manages an alert alone.

2. Provenance-Separated Vitals & Claim-to-Source Ledger:

As the user explores their physiological telemetry tracking simulated resting heart rate (72 bpm), SpO₂ (98%), core temperature (36.8 °C), 24 hour wellness trends, and cycle-ergometer Lead II ECG waveforms, every insight is visibly separated from published mission references (such as the 1.84 mSv/day Mars-cruise GCR reference).

By opening the Claim-to-Source Ledger, the user can inspect 8 peer-reviewed claims and 5 NASA/CSA resources, each explicitly stating what the evidence supports and what it "DOES NOT PROVE" (such as clarifying that NASA OSDR dataset OSD-288 is murine spleen RNA-seq, not a human clinical diagnosis).

3. Interactive Mission Simulation & Closed-Loop Orchestrator:

Through the Orbit & Space-Weather Monitor, users can test 8 mission scenarios: Nominal Cruise, Solar Flare, Hypoxia Risk, Bio-Loop Fault, Neuro-Fatigue, Dehydration, Bone & Muscle, and Immune Risk.

• During a Solar Flare Event (Scenario B), live NASA DONKI space-weather context triggers an immediate Action Prompt: the system locks microalgae biomass release to prevent radiation contamination, prioritizes crew sheltering, and queues pre-clinical candidates (such as phycocyanin-rich Arthrospira platensis under prototype rule ABS-RAD-04) strictly for later laboratory review rather than automated dosing.

• Gamified Bio-Dome Stewardship: To combat isolation and monotony, the dashboard includes a Green Finger Score (94/100) and "Oxygen Cycle Guardian" milestone that reward consistent care of the onboard microalgae culture.

4. Transparent Mass-Balance Bioreactor Model:

Users can interactively adjust engineering parameters reactor working volume (250 L), biomass productivity (0.4 g/L/day), oxygen yield (1.5 g O₂/g biomass), and crew size (4 people) to calculate daily biomass (100.0 g/day) and oxygen contribution (150.0 g/day, supporting 4.5% of crew demand within a ±25% uncertainty band), reinforcing engineering transparency over medical guesswork.

Who Benefits & Dual-Use Impact (Sarawak Research Bridge)

AstroBio Sentinel benefits astronauts, flight surgeons, researchers, and rural communities by:

• Protecting Deep-Space Crews: Reducing cognitive load and automation bias during long-duration missions where real-time Earth consultation is impossible.

• Advancing Sustainable Biotechnology (SDG 12): Connecting closed-loop spacecraft life support with Sarawak’s tropical microalgae research pathway (Arthrospira platensis, Chlorella, and Haematococcus pluvialis).

• Supporting Rural Healthcare (SDG 3 & SDG 9): Adapting offline, low-bandwidth vital-sign tracking to help remote clinics in Sarawak monitor patients safely during internet or power outages.

Our Goal & Current Limitations

Our goal is to make NASA’s open space-health data actionable, transparent, and safe for autonomous human exploration while inspiring dual-use innovation in Sarawak. Despite its comprehensive evidence ledger, our current prototype relies on simulated biometric inputs rather than live flight-certified wearable hardware, and our usability evaluation protocol (targeting 5–10 pilot participants using task-completion time, error rate, and NASA-TLX workload scores) is designed as our immediate next validation milestone.

Tools, Data Sources & Technologies Used

• Frontend & Web Technologies: React, TypeScript, HTML5, and CSS (generated and hosted via Figma Make / Figma Sites) powering the offline-first interactive dashboard, 8 mission simulations, and real-time Mass-Balance bioreactor calculator directly in the browser.

• Mission Landing Page & Audio Hosting: Framer (used to build the companion mission overview website and distress communications audio player).

• Space-Weather API Integration: JavaScript REST API Connector fetching live solar-flare status from NASA DONKI while keeping simulated crew values strictly separate.

• NASA & Space Agency Data Sources:

- NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / OSD-288): Used spaceflight transcriptomics data to anchor cellular stress boundaries.

- NASA DONKI: Integrated live solar-flare space-weather monitoring separate from simulated prototype states.

- NASA Human Research Program (HRP): Mapped "5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight", "Risks of Human Spaceflight", and "Ongoing HRP Research in Space" directly into the interface.

- Canadian Space Agency (CSA): Referenced astronaut radiation monitoring and space science resources.

• Visual & Audio Assets: Official Framer and Figma templates, original profile and audio thumbnails created manually by the author, and select SI-assisted graphics (algae, laboratory equipment, and mission maps generated via Figma AI).

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

AstroBio Sentinel was conceptualized, researched, and structured by a solo creator, with the Framer companion page built manually without SI tools. SI tools were utilized transparently in a supportive capacity:

• Design & Visuals: Figma AI assisted with UI layout alignment and generated select prototype graphics (algae, laboratory equipment, and mission maps, clearly labeled with SI-generated indicators).

• Audio Narration: ElevenLabs AI generated the English voiceover for the 30-second demonstration video (acknowledged in video captions and metadata).

• Research & Editing: Consensus aided in locating peer-reviewed radiobiology and wearable-sensor literature (manually verified by the author), while Google AI assisted with English grammar polishing.
